text:
Sam (Support): hey @acme_dev — following up on the oauth failures you reported. you said both GitHub and Google logins are failing with a state mismatch on the callback? can you paste the exact error you see in the browser and any callback URL used?
acme_dev (Customer): yes, on our web app users hit the oauth provider, auth screen, then after approve we get redirected back to our callback and the app shows: "AuthError: state verification failed". stacktrace from client: `AuthError: state mismatch` and server logs show `callback_handler: state_mismatch expected=YwLq... got=YwLq%2B...` (note the plus -> %2B). redirect URI we register: `https://app.acme.example/auth/callback` (no trailing slash).
Sam (Support): thanks — do you also see anything in network console like the querystring on the callback? sometimes proxies or SPA routers rewrite/encode params.
acme_dev (Customer): yes, network tab shows the callback: `https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?state=YwLq%2Babc&code=...` but our server expected raw base64url string (no padding, no +). we generate PKCE verifier client-side with `crypto.getRandomValues` and base64url encode; on mobile we use the native browser flow.
Priya (Eng): couple of quick checks: 1) confirm you use base64url (RFC 4648 §5) for code_challenge — that forbids `+` and `/` and should remove `=` padding. 2) ensure your app doesn't re-encode an already-encoded state (double-encoding will turn `+` into `%2B`). 3) check any reverse proxy (CF, nginx) for `ignore_invalid_headers` or URL-normalize settings that might alter `+` characters.
acme_dev (Customer): we use CloudFront + ALB in front. could CF be converting + -> %2B? seems odd.
Marcus (SRE): CF sometimes treats `+` as space in logs but it shouldn't mutate path/query. however if a redirect is going through a lambda edge that urlencodes params manually we could end up double-encoding. also check if any middleware is calling `encodeURIComponent` on the full querystring. that would encode the `%` leading to `%252B` (seen as `%2B` when decoded once).
Priya (Eng): also confirm how you store state between initial auth request and callback. do you keep the raw state server-side (session DB) or rely on the client echoing it back? best practice: store a short nonce server-side keyed to session id and compare the stored value against the returned state instead of comparing raw long PKCE strings.
acme_dev (Customer): we store the full state in a session cookie and match on callback. cookie set like `Set-Cookie: session=...; SameSite=Lax; Secure; HttpOnly`. could SameSite cause issues for cross-site redirects? some browsers treat third-party redirects differently, esp during SSO flows.
Sam (Support): good point. for OAuth redirect flows SameSite=Lax should be OK for top-level navigation, but certain embedded webviews or Safari ITP may block cookies. I recommend testing with a short state hash stored server-side as Marcus suggested so callback doesn't rely on cookie availability.
Priya (Eng): one more thing — if you see plus signs in server log expected vs actual, try logging the raw bytes before any URL-decoding. example from our debug kit: `logger.debug('raw_query', req.url)` and `logger.debug('state_raw', req.query.state)` — compare both.
acme_dev (Customer): we did that. raw req.url shows `?state=YwLq+abc` but req.query.state shows `YwLq%2Babc`. so it looks like express or our proxy is decoding differently.
Marcus (SRE): aligns with proxy double-encoding theory. actionable: 1) search for `encodeURI`/`encodeURIComponent` in edge lambdas and CDN behaviors; 2) temporarily switch to a simplified test route that echoes back the request querystring (no middleware) to confirm where the mutation happens; 3) try short-lived workaround: on initial auth request, compute `state_hash = sha256(state)` and store that server-side; return the long state to provider but validate the returned state's hash on callback. that makes the server immune to small encoding differences as long as you canonicalize.
Priya (Eng): example canonicalization snippet (js):
```
function canonicalState(s) {
  // interpret plus as literal plus and normalize percent-encoding
  return decodeURIComponent(s.replace(/\+/g, '%2B'));
}
```
use cautiously — better to avoid needing it by fixing the root encoding step.
Sam (Support): has someone tried reproducing from a clean environment (no CDN) to isolate component? can you reproduce with curl to the callback? example curl we ask for:
```
curl -i 'https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?state=YwLq%2Babc&code=foo'
```
what does your app log for `expected` vs `received`?
acme_dev (Customer): curl to ALB (bypassing CF) returns expected=YwLq+abc, received=YwLq+abc (works). curl to CF domain returns expected=YwLq+abc, received=YwLq%2Babc (fail). looks like CF edge lambda or behavior is the culprit.
Marcus (SRE): ok that isolates it. check your CloudFront behaviours: are you forwarding querystring and all headers? if you have any function that manipulates querystring or uses `encodeURIComponent` on the composed URL for a redirect it will double-encode `%`. also check if `ViewerProtocolPolicy` or `OriginRequestPolicy` rewrites are in place.
Priya (Eng): mitigation options: 1) fix the CF lambda to avoid re-encoding; 2) canonicalize on callback (decode once, then compare) — canonicalization must be implemented carefully to avoid security regressions; 3) switch to using a short server-side nonce (recommended).
acme_dev (Customer): thanks — we'll patch the edge lambda. curious if Redwood has any standard advice for mobile custom scheme callbacks? we saw a similar issue on iOS where `+` got converted to space when using `myapp://auth?state=...`.
Sam (Support): for mobile custom schemes it's common to percent-encode everything after scheme on redirect and ensure the app decodes on receive. also prefer `state` values that are url-safe (hex or base64url without padding). many teams hash the PKCE verifier to produce a URL-safe truncated nonce.
Priya (Eng): final notes: ensure `code_challenge_method` is `S256` (not `plain`) and that your `code_verifier` generation uses url-safe base64 without `=`. sample PKCE gen (browser):
```
const rand = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
const b64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...rand)).replace(/\+/g,'-').replace(/\//g,'_').replace(/=+$/,'');
```
Sam (Support): I'll log this thread and include a short repro checklist for you. tagging @Marcus so SRE can review CF lambda.
Marcus (SRE): got it — I'll check lambda code for any `encodeURIComponent` calls and the CloudFront function logs. will follow up here with findings.
acme_dev (Customer): thanks everyone — will update after we patch and test. :thumbsup:
